gljs/render-tests/terrain/fill-extrusion: Over terrain, a ground-level wall's foot reaches the ground under its own end; GL JS stops it 10 m below the ground at the polygon's centroid, which leaves a gap under the downhill walls of this fixture's buildings, 450 m wide on a mountainside. 165 of 262,144 px differ, all along the feet of the two buildings' south walls, which now reach the slope; 8 differed before the feet followed the ground
gljs/render-tests/terrain/heatmap: Over terrain, GL JS colors each tile's kernel density on its own and blends the tiles, so where kernels of two tiles overlap their density doesn't add up; mln-rs adds it up across tiles, as both do without terrain. The kernels stand where GL JS draws them; 1,552 of 262,144 px differ, all where kernels of the fixture's two GeoJSON tiles overlap
